s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent episodes of hypertension with associated palpitations and diaphoresis, suggesting a catecholamine-excess state, with a history of adrenal mass and positive family history suggestive of a hereditary syndrome
salient_findings: Presence of a nodule in the left adrenal bed on Gallium 68-DOTATATE PET scan
Prostatic lesion with increased size over time
key_facts: Initial presentation at age 18 years in 1984
10-cm mass of the organ of Zukerkandl in 1984
Presentation with palpitations and diaphoresis in 2014
Positive Gallium 68-DOTATATE PET scan with a nodule in the left adrenal bed
Prostatic lesion increased in size from 1.9 cm in 2014 to 2.9 cm in 2021
Tumors positive for GATA3, tyrosine hydroxylase, chromogranin A, and synaptophysin on immunohistochemistry

shortlist.label: Succinate dehydrogenase B-related paraganglioma
shortlist.why_kept: SDHB gene variant and history of paraganglioma

shortlist.label: Pheochromocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated 24-hour urinary normetanephrine and history of adrenal mass

shortlist.label: Paraganglioma
shortlist.why_kept: Positive Gallium 68-DOTATATE PET scan with a nodule in the left adrenal bed

shortlist.label: Prostatic paraganglioma
shortlist.why_kept: Prostatic lesion with increased size and positive immunohistochemistry results

shortlist.label: Familial paraganglioma
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent episodes of hypertension and family history suggestive of a hereditary syndrome

raw.rationale: The patient has a SDHB gene variant: c.338G>A (p.C113Y), which is a known mutation associated with hereditary paragangliomas, and the presence of a mass in the organ of Zukerkandl and a nodule in the left adrenal bed, along with elevated urinary normetanephrine, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pheochromocytoma
rejected.why: While pheochromocytoma could explain some symptoms, the presence of the SDHB gene variant and the specific tumor locations point more towards paraganglioma.

rejected.label: Paraganglioma
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes the champion diagnosis; the specific SDHB mutation and clinical presentation make Succinate dehydrogenase B-related paraganglioma more precise.

rejected.label: Prostatic paraganglioma
rejected.why: Although there is a prostatic lesion, the primary issue seems to be related to the paraganglioma in the adrenal bed, and the prostatic lesion may be a metastasis or a separate but related finding.

rejected.label: Familial paraganglioma
rejected.why: The diagnosis of Succinate dehydrogenase B-related paraganglioma already implies a familial component due to the genetic mutation, making this option less specific than the champion diagnosis.
